sentences.text: Revenue grew from $38.5 billion in FY2016 to $67.6 billion in FY2025, a 6.4% compound rate [F1][F10][F201].
Revenue fell 22.4% in FY2020 as lower sales volume reflected weaker end-user demand, and operating margin dropped 4.5pp to 10.9% [D198][P59][D211][F25].
FY2023's 6.0pp margin gain to 19.3% was attributed to favorable price realization and higher sales volume [D370][F28][P31].
Operating income compounded at 28.6%, far faster than revenue, so margin expansion did most of the work [F202][F201].
Power Energy supplied the largest FY2025 contribution, adding 5.2pp of the 4.3% revenue growth and reaching 47.6% of revenue [D759][D463][D757].
Its Power Generation unit grew 32.5% and added 3.9pp, while Construction Industries fell 1.6% and subtracted 0.6pp [D894][D895][D765][D766].
The filing attributes the 4.3% rise to higher equipment volume sold to end users, though not Power Generation specifically [D463][P13].
Operating income fell 14.7% on 4.3% revenue growth, an incremental margin of -69.1% [D464][D463][D488].
Diluted EPS fell 14.7%, less than the 17.7% net income drop, as the diluted share count fell 3.5% [D467][D465][D483].
Operating margin of 16.5% in FY2025 sits above the 14.3% window median and below the 20.2% FY2024 high [F30][D1123][D1122].
Cost of revenue reached 66.2% of revenue from 62.0%, cutting 4.2pp from operating margin [D441][D388][D490].
Operating income fell from $13.1 billion to $11.2 billion, which the filing attributes to higher tariff-linked manufacturing costs and unfavorable price realization [F19][F20][P9][P17].
Net margin of 13.1% sits 3.4pp below operating margin, with the effective tax rate up to 24.0% from 19.7% [F50][F30][D449][D396].
Tariffs are the stated cause, so margin recovery depends more on that cost line than on volume [P17].
Free cash flow of $8.9 billion equalled 1.00x net income, against a window median of 0.96x [F100][D451][D1135].
Free cash flow margin of 13.2% sits above the 11.9% window median and below the 16.8% FY2023 high [D447][D1129][D1128].
Within Machinery, Power & Energy, operating cash flow rose on lower working capital needs and lower cash taxes [P4].
Capex of $2.8 billion was 1.25x D&A and 4.2% of revenue, and the filing cites higher capital expenditures in MP&E investing outflows [F90][D452][D446][P3].
Net debt reached $26.2 billion in FY2025, up from $22.1 billion in FY2023, or 38.8% of revenue [D456][D350][D457].
Net cash at -38.8% of revenue ranks 43rd percentile among seven industrials peers, against a peer median of -35.6% [D457][D1151][D1152].
Long-term debt rose 12.2% to $30.7 billion, and the filing attributes Financial Products' financing inflow to intercompany and external borrowings [D474][F190][P2].
Buybacks of $5.2 billion and dividends of $2.7 billion absorbed 89.0% of free cash flow, while diluted shares fell 3.5% [X140][X150][D459][D483].
Net cash has fallen two years running into net debt, the medium-severity flag R1, and the filing ties the borrowing to Financial Products [R1][D456][P2].
Operating income fell 14.7% on 4.3% revenue growth, a single-year operating-leverage flag with a -69.1% incremental margin [D464][D463][D488].
FY2025 net income is proxy-sourced rather than from the 10-K, but both figures round to $8.9 billion [F40][X20][R3].
Dropped R2: the FY2024 revenue decline of 3.4% was followed by 4.3% growth in FY2025 [D410][D463].
Operating margin below the 14.3% window median in the FY2026 10-K would confirm the tariff squeeze is persisting [D1123][F30][P14].
Net debt wider than the FY2025 level of $26.2 billion in the FY2026 10-K would extend the two-year widening [D456].
Free cash flow above the 0.96x window median of net income in the FY2026 10-K would confirm conversion is holding through the margin squeeze [D451][D1135].
